the ejected mass of type I supernovæ varies by at least a factor of two, the amount of synthesized nickel-56 varies by at least an order of magnitude, and the bolometric light curve shape varies by a factor of ten.

the progenitor system for some type Ias may be sub Chandrasekhar, and that a significant range of the observed bolometric light curve can be attributed to the progenitor and explosion physics.

there are significant variations in the progenitor system properties, the explosion mechanism, and the subsequent radiation transport.
the bolometric light curves of type I supernovæ provide a powerful tool to constrain the progenitor system and explosion mechanism.
